content_blocks.title: Core idea
content_blocks.text: GitHub Actions secrets are protected configuration values scoped to repositories, environments, or organizations; access depends on context and policy. Security starts with least privilege and trust boundaries: scope tokens, store credentials as secrets, isolate untrusted contributions, and prefer short-lived federated credentials when available. The most useful check is one that produces observable evidence and fails clearly when its stated requirement is not met.

items.title: What a secret is
items.text: Store credentials in the appropriate protected secret store, pass them only to the step that needs them, and never print or save them in logs, summaries, artifacts, or caches.

content_blocks.code:
name: Check a required secret without revealing it
on: workflow_dispatch
permissions:
  contents: read
jobs:
  validate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Validate credential configuration
        env:
          API_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.API_TOKEN }}
        run: test -n "$API_TOKEN"
content_blocks.expected_output: The check succeeds when the protected `API_TOKEN` secret is present and fails otherwise. It does not print the credential; use a test secret in a controlled repository.
content_blocks.run_instructions: Use a test repository or static validation first. Confirm the secret/variable scope and permissions match your environment before a real run.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Remove the temporary workflow and revoke test credentials or app installations when finished.

content_blocks.title: Recap

troubleshooting: If a workflow never starts, verify the workflow is under `.github/workflows/`, the event and filters match, and repository/organization Actions policy allows it.
If a step fails, inspect the first failed step, exit code, stderr, installed tool versions, permissions, and runner/network state before retrying.
If a job is skipped or data is missing, inspect `if`, `needs`, outputs, artifact names/paths, and cache keys; jobs do not automatically share filesystems.
common_mistakes: Assuming YAML parsing proves the workflow runs correctly or matches the intended trigger.
Granting broad token permissions, printing environment values, or exposing a secret to untrusted code.
Using a placeholder command as evidence of a real build, test, deployment, or security scan.
